title: Ops Runway: SLO Integration & Sprint Checklist (Q2 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical, cross-functional checklist and sprint-ready pack to integrate SLOs into product/service delivery cycles. It is intentionally lightweight — meant to be used as a working artifact during an "Ops Runway" workshop and as a cookbook teams can copy into their sprint backlogs.

High-level goals:
- Create end-to-end process for defining, validating, and shipping SLO-backed changes for a service.
- Make measurement pipelines and alerting part of the feature rollout rather than an afterthought.
- Give product, infra, and SRE clear entry/exit criteria for each sprint.

Scope (what this checklist covers):
- SLO definition and baseline estimation
- Measurement pipeline (metrics, tags, retention)
- Alerting thresholds and runbooks
- Canary/rollout policy and automated fallback
- Post-deployment quality checks and quick evals
- Documentation, ownership, and handoff to on-call

Who should use this pack:
- Product leads and PMs shipping user-facing changes that affect request volumes or latency
- Backend/service owners and infra engineers introducing config or runtime changes
- SRE/observability owning SLOs and platform monitoring
- Release engineering responsible for canaries and rollbacks

Quick glossary (for workshop newcomers):
- SLI: Signal used to measure user experience (p99 latency, successful response rate)
- SLO: Target for an SLI over a window (99.9% success rate / 30d)
- Error budget: Allowable SLO violations consumed by releases or incidents
- Measurement pipeline: The set of metrics collection, aggregation, and retention that produces SLIs

Pre-work (to run before the Ops Runway workshop):
1) Service owners attach current endpoint list and traffic split to the agenda doc. (owner: service PM)
2) SRE exports last 90 days of candidate SLIs (latency histograms, success rates, user-facing errors). (owner: observability team)
3) Release engineer prepares current canary tooling checklist and previous rollbacks. (owner: release-eng)
4) Identify stakeholders for the 2-week integration sprint and invite them to the kickoff. (owner: PM)

Ops Runway Workshop agenda (2.5 hrs):
- 00:00–00:15: Context and goals — why SLO integration matters for this service (PM + SRE)
- 00:15–00:40: Data review — SLIs, traffic shifts, historical violations (observability)
- 00:40–01:10: Define candidate SLOs, windows, and error budget policy (group exercise)
- 01:10–01:35: Measurement: metrics, labels, retention, and dashboards required (infra + SRE)
- 01:35–02:00: Canary & rollout policy: success/fail gates, traffic ramp schedule, automated rollback triggers (release-eng)
- 02:00–02:20: Runbook sketch & escalation path (on-call + product)
- 02:20–02:30: Sprint plan and owners — who does what in the next 2 sprints

Checklist (to be turned into sprint tickets):
A. SLO & SLI definition (ticket examples)
- ticket: sli:define (owner: service-SRE)
  - description: list SLI metrics, aggregation windows, tags (customer-id, region), query definitions
  - acceptance: dashboard visualizes raw SLI and aggregated SLO window with baseline overlay

B. Baseline & error budget (ticket: slo:baseline)
- calculate 30d/90d baseline, show seasonality, simulate error budget burn under projected traffic
- acceptance: baseline doc + spreadsheet attached to ticket with burn simulation and sensitivity notes

C. Measurement ingestion (ticket: metrics:pipe)
- implement metrics export (histogram summaries), add tags, instrument latency buckets for p50/p95/p99
- ensure retention policy meets SLO windows; add cardinality guards for user-tagged labels
- acceptance: CI job verifies metric coverage and new metrics appear on staging dashboards

D. Alerting & runbooks (ticket: alert:prep)
- author alert rules: golden signal alerts for SLI deviation and error budget burn rate
- define paging policy and playbook steps (who to call, mitigation knobs, short-term patches)
- acceptance: test alert fire in staging and walk through runbook with on-call (recorded)

E. Canary policy & automation (ticket: rollout:canary)
- automated ramp steps (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% every 15m), pass/fail criteria (SLO delta, errors), rollback automated via orchestration
- include test plan for load/chaos scenarios to validate canary gating
- acceptance: canary run recorded in staging with intentional failure to validate rollback path

F. Documentation & handoff (ticket: docs:handoff)
- update service README with SLO definitions, alert contact list, and deck link
- schedule 30-minute handoff session with on-call and product
- acceptance: on-call marks "handoff complete" with checklist ticked in ticket

Sprint template (copy into backlog):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): Pre-work tasks A + B + small metrics pipe changes; define canary policy
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): Finish measurement pipeline, alerts & runbooks, automation for canary
- Sprint 3 (if needed): Hardening, long-tail metrics, production rollout and verification

RACI (short text version)
- Responsible: service owner (definitions), observability eng (metrics), release eng (canary), SRE (alerts/runbooks)
- Accountable: eng manager of service
- Consulted: product manager, security (if changes to auth/data), compliance (if retention changes)
- Informed: customer-success, support, exec reporting

Pass/fail gates & quick checks (to automate where possible):
- Gate 1 (pre-canary): metric coverage >= 95% of user traffic in staging
- Gate 2 (during canary): error budget burn rate in last 30m < threshold OR no increase in user-facing error rate by >X%
- Gate 3 (post-rollout 24h): p99 latency within defined SLO ±10% and no new class of 5xx errors

Risk register (sample):
- High cardinality tags accidentally introduced -> mitigation: cardinality review and guard rails in metrics:pipe ticket
- Measurement drift (instrumentation change) -> mitigation: include semantic metric versioning and a "golden query" to baseline
- Canary automation failing silently -> mitigation: require explicit test run in staging and alert on orchestration failures

Communications plan (who to notify and when):
- Pre-rollout: Slack channel #svc-ops, email to support and CS (24h before)
- During canary: observability bot posts signal health; 15m cadence updates to the channel
- Post-rollout: summary note to #product-launch and weekly reliability digest with error budget consumption

Acceptance criteria for "SLO integrated into release":
- Metrics pipeline produces SLIs in prod and staging and dashboards show current windows
- Canary automation enforces pass/fail gates and rollback worked in a test run
- Runbook exists and on-call can execute mitigation steps (verified runbook drill)
- Product owner has signed off on SLO & error budget policy

Next steps (for the first integration run):
1) Book Ops Runway workshop (owner: Aisha) — target week of Apr 11, 2026
2) Create backlog tickets using the checklist above and tag them with JIRA-OPS-1248
3) Run a staged canary in staging and force a rollback to validate automation (owner: release-eng)
4) Schedule handoff with on-call and product (owner: PM)

Notes to keep in this doc (living):
- Keep examples of query definitions for p99 latency, success ratio, and user-visible errors (appendix)
- Add a short template for "intentional rollback test" that teams can copy to CI
- Track lessons learned after each integration with date + name + short summary

Appendix: example SLI queries (staging) — copy/paste ready:
- success_rate = sum(rate(http_success_total{service="svc-a"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="svc-a"}[5m]))
- p99_latency_ms = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="svc-a"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000

End of doc.
